A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GROTO study, and their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. v1 contains the main paper and references; v2 additionally includes Supplementary Material, Sections 6–15.

before.justification: v1 reports original GROTO benchmark results, component ablations, sensitivity experiments and feature visualizations in Tables 1–5 and Figures 3–6.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds DomainNet evaluation, class-discovery diagnostics, further ablations and measured computational costs.

M1.justification: Equation 11 corrects the contrastive-loss denominator from repeatedly using the augmented sample x_i' to using batch sample x_b. The architecture, prototype selection, replay and PTD losses otherwise remain stable. Algorithm 3 still prints the earlier denominator, so this establishes a correction to the stated loss, not a verified implementation change.

E1.justification: Section 8 adds DomainNet-126-CI evaluation across twelve transfers involving Clipart, Painting, Sketch and Real domains. This substantially expands the evaluated object populations and visual domains beyond the three retained benchmarks.

E2.justification: For the P→A old-class-retention comparison, v1 Figure 3 evaluates DIFO, LEAD-B and LCFD, whereas v2 Table 11 reports CIDA, DIFO and LCFD. Thus comparator membership changes within that diagnostic, although the main comparison sets in Tables 1–3 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The original benchmarks retain their stated session construction, optimizer settings and accuracy metrics. Added experiments introduce six alphabetical 20-class sessions for DomainNet, PCD/TCD class-discovery metrics, and feature-space and resource measurements. These extend evaluation procedures without establishing revisions to the retained experiments.

E4.justification: Table 4 newly isolates coarse versus fine prototypes and the contrastive, compactness and separability losses. Supplementary Sections 9–10 add quantitative class-mining diagnostics, broader forgetting analyses and source/target feature comparisons; Section 15 adds efficiency analysis. The prototype-selection visualization formerly included in Figure 5 is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The retained prediction-confidence standard deviation used to select prototypes is a method component, not uncertainty reporting for experimental results.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their numerical results. Table 3 revises LEAD-B's Office-Home session average from 68.0 to 70.4, and Figure 6 revises the displayed without/with-PTD accuracies from 93.8/96.4 to 96.5/99.4. Substantial new results include DomainNet averages of 65.7 for GROTO, 62.5 for LCFD and 43.5 for DIFO, plus component, class-mining, forgetting and resource results.

T1.justification: Section 15.1 and Table 15 add computational-complexity derivations for ViT-B and GROTO's modules. Equation 11 also receives a mathematical correction. The problem assumptions and PTD equations remain unchanged, and no theorem or proof framework is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstracts, contribution lists and conclusions retain the CI-SFUDA problem, GROTO's two principal modules, reduced forgetting and state-of-the-art performance claims. The supplementary evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Section 10 newly explains that preserving compatibility with source classifiers can favor source-like features over optimal target representations, producing a compactness tradeoff. Section 3.4 also explains why compactness loss alone can discard patterns and why separability loss helps balance mappings. These qualify the retained mechanism interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 supplies Algorithms 1–5, exact session class lists, RTX 3090 hardware, momentum and weight decay, prototype-balancing details, exemplar-refresh intervals, augmentation choices and resource measurements. These substantially fill documentation gaps in v1; they do not establish that the underlying implementation or existing experimental settings changed.

R1.justification: v2 substantially refreshes the SFDA/CIL literature and explicitly positions GROTO against unsupervised class-incremental learning that does not handle domain shifts. It also newly connects the PTD motivation to prototype-oriented domain adaptation and conditional transport through references 36 and 48, while removing numerous earlier citations.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, PTD explanation and experimental discussion undergo extensive rewriting. Separate SFUDA and SF-UniDA discussions are consolidated, definitions are relocated, and an organized supplement adds detailed algorithmic and experimental explanations. Author information and acknowledgements also change.

P2.justification: Table 4 expands, and the supplement adds Tables 6–16, Algorithms 1–5 and Figures 7–9, including expansions of retained plots. Figures 3 and 6 are revised. Figure 5 enlarges the feature-distribution plots while removing the prototype panel, although its caption still refers to that panel.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves reproducibility through explicit training procedures and session class assignments, and strengthens support for design choices through finer Table 4 ablations and supplementary class-mining, forgetting and DomainNet evaluations. The newly discussed PTD tradeoff also improves interpretation. The Equation 11/Algorithm 3 disagreement and stale Figure 5 caption limit clarity, but do not outweigh these substantial gains over v1.
